title: The Abandoned Arcade Where Games Dream of Players

features.name: ticket window
features.desc-on-touch: The booth where players used to exchange money for tokens. Now the drawer is half-open and empty. Your fingers trace the scratches where coins rested for years.

features.name: dreaming cabinet
features.desc-on-touch: The game still has power from somewhere. Its screen blinks once per minute, showing a character standing alone on an empty stage, waiting for input that will never come.

features.name: token hopper
features.desc-on-touch: The machine's hopper is jammed with tokens it will never give to anyone. It tried once, they say, in 1996. Only silence came back from the floor.

features.name: watchers' bench
features.desc-on-touch: Worn velour holds the shape of people who don't come anymore. Some initials carved in the frame. Empty drink bottles still wedged underneath. The bench remembers.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the low-view afternoon
narr: She sits on the bench beside you, watching the game
you've already lost. The cabinet hums its small song.
She says: they kept playing after everyone left.
Nobody told the machines. So they still wait.
You feel the bench hold two shapes at once,
one present, one still coming home.

inscription: the games still dream: someone will return and understand them again
